beats.lead: Guinness World Records credits this game with a very specific first
beats.text: It was not the first battery-saved game.
beats.note: The Legend of Zelda, 1986, is officially the first game with a battery as part of the cartridge. That wording is precise because it has to be.

beats.name: Pop and Chips
beats.role: An obscure Super Cassette Vision game that used a battery backup a year before Zelda. Nintendo itself had used the concept even earlier, in a 1984 programming add-on.

beats.lead: So what did Zelda actually do first
beats.note: Earlier battery-backed cartridges needed players to load their own bulky AA batteries. Zelda hid a slim button cell inside a cartridge that looked completely ordinary, saving up to three files.

beats.text: That one hidden battery helped kill Nintendo's own disk drive.

beats.line: Not the first save. The first save you couldn't see.
